content.text:
This site has a light and a dark theme and follows the visitor's system setting. Build both from its extracted tokens, switched with `prefers-color-scheme`.

Required, in this order, before you present any UI:
1. Design system: keep the product's own design whenever it has one. In a codebase with its own theme file, tokens or component library, build with those, read their values with `extract-design-system` if you need them, and never install a catalog system over them. For a product with a live site, call `extract-from-url` on that site before you build: it is required, never skipped. With no code at hand, its tokens are its design: use its colours, surfaces, borders, font and radius, and keep the type at app scale, not the site's display sizes. When `extract-from-url` returns both themes, ship both, switched with `prefers-color-scheme`. When it returns one theme, ship only that scheme. Use the brand's own `primary` from `extract-from-url` for actions and the selected state. When it reports no primary, the brand has no colour accent: fill the main button with its text colour and label it in its background colour. Never pick a hue of your own, such as red, blue or indigo. Only a product with no design of its own installs a catalog system with `get-design-system-kit`, choosing one whose colour scheme matches the brand: a light brand gets a light system and a dark brand a dark one, even when a system of the other scheme ranks first.
2. Principles: call `get-ui-principle` before styling and `get-ux-principle` before behavior.
3. Build with those tokens and principles. A product screen sits inside the product's app shell: navigation with the product's real sections, the current one active, and the workspace or project it belongs to. Show the summary, the records and the selected record's detail together, not behind tabs. Keep the summary to the few numbers a working user acts on: one leads, the rest sit beside it as plain figures or in the page header, never a default row of identical stat cards. The detail shows the full record a working user checks, not a summary of it: for a trace, every span by its real name in a timed waterfall, the selected span's attributes, and model, tokens and cost. Use the record's own names and fields from the product's docs, and give each action one place on the screen. Fill it with realistic sample data, including the metrics, IDs and fields a working user would see: sample data in a product screen is not an invented claim. Only claims about the company itself, such as customers, results and endorsements, must stay real. The main button always looks active: a solid fill and a full-contrast label, never a grey or faded fill. Only a control that is truly disabled looks disabled. Mark a selected row or the active navigation item with a fill, the brand primary at low opacity or the surface's selected tint, never a coloured edge, underline or outline. Keep the page title at app scale, the size of a section heading, not a marketing display. Keep each table row on one line by dropping low-value columns. Truncate only IDs and long free text, never the labels people scan.
4. Review: where `review-ui-code` is available, run it on every file you wrote, a one-file HTML page included, after your last edit: send each file's path and no content, so it reads the whole file. Then call `get-review-rules`, then `check-comprehension` with the page's real copy, and `inspect-spacing` on the rendered page. Fix every critical and serious finding.
Do not present a page that skipped step 2 or step 4. If a step fails, say which one.



...(truncated to ~0 tokens)

What this sheet does not carry: an oversized blurred gradient, a frosted panel, a glow, a stagger on load, an easing curve. When the user points at an effect like that, read it as a layer stack with `get-ui-principle({ topic: "reading-a-reference" })`. Label each claim Measured, Derived, or Inferred. Then rebuild it in the user's project from the owning principle, with these tokens.
